title: HUANUO Single Monitor Mount, Monitor Arm for 13”-32” Monitors up to 17.6 lbs, Adjustable Stand with 16” Max Height, Desk Mount with C-Clamp and Grommet Base, VESA 75x75mm or 100x100mm
reviews: Not gonna lie I was kinda nervous after reading other reviews about weak joints/mount and thankfully I’ve had none of those issues. Each part that moves feels solid but not too strong that you’d have to fight with it. The actual VESA mount part mounts just fine to the monitor but that part does feel a little tight that it would be hard to move the monitor up or down so I have to use the Allen key that’s included to move it up or down.Moving the arm forward,backwards,left or right feels sturdy but smooth and at no point do I feel like it might not be secure. The actual c clamp part that mounts to the desk is a prettt thick piece of metal that wont come loose or wobble and has a foam lining so it doesn’t scratch or dig into your desk. Included are three little clips for cable management, 2 for the horizontal arm and one for the vertical pole. Overall a good monitor mount and if I get a second monitor I’ll definitely be buying another mount. One minor complaint is the vesa mount on the monitor slides into the arm but it’s not a precise fit so the monitor is ever so slightly off angle but it’s an easy enough fix that a tiny piece of cardboard can take care of.
I really love these monitor stands. They're great, super sturdy even on a not so sturdy desk. They hold my 32-in monitors. Great and I absolutely love them!.

After looking around for display mount I decided to go with a monitor arm. I'm currently renting, so the less wholes I make, the less I have to patch up. But this arm works perfect for me, more leg room, meaning that I have more room on my desk and less clutter including the monitor legs or stand since its now higher and off the desk by the arm. Easy to assemble and no special tool needed, the only thing I wish they used better cap screws, the ones on these are a bit short and not well made on the inside. I try using the allen key that came with it, but using a small amount of strength and it just slides off the cap and started to bent. Luckily it didn't need allot of tying up, just a small amount for the monitor mount.

Not good at all. The monitor will tilt down and continue to do so no matter what I do. I've tried tightening the angle bolt so hard that my hand hurts. My screen is well within specs - around 9lbs so less than half of the maximum, yet it still can't hold. The screws are also the wrong length so they stick out the back ever so much and create a horrible grinding sounds anytime the monitor moves forward or back on them from the mount. These were the M4-30mm provided used on an Asus curved monitor. Assembly was fine, but adjustments are a pain, requiring the Allen wrench for height and angle. I will sadly be going through the effort of dismantling it, putting my stand back on, packaging it up, and returning it to get my money back on something that didn't work. I even went through the process of buying a wood block so the clamp would fit under my desk :(

Giving this 4 Stars because of the tension issue with the vertical angle of the monitors. As a quick fix for anyone who has the same issue of the monitor sagging. Just loosen the bolt rip a business card in half and stick it in both sides and tighten it hard! Fixed it and now its sitting level and even. Anyway for 20 dollars I can't complain since its working now. 12lb Monitor for reference.

I really love this monitor stand. Especially the price. It is exactly what I need. 90% of the time, I like to have my monitor in portrait mode, to display page text better. I have a 24" monitor, and can view 2x2 pages scrolling. I also enjoy coding using a portrait layout. And viewing web pages. Most things actually. For some graphic design, photos, systems that only have a cli, etc, a normal landscape view is better. I wish I had purchased this sooner. I did use some shorter screws with the provided mounting bracket standoffs. One set of provided screws were too short, the other provided set was too long. This has nothing to do with arm, just how my monitor is. There was very little in the way of assembly, and that was easy and straightforward. documentation was good. All motion/pivot points are smooth. Rotation point appeared locked at first. I contacted vendor, they responded promptly. I applied a little more force and it broke free, and now rotates (smooth but stiff, as it should be) I will probably be replacing all of my factory monitor stands with these.

Full disclosure: I was attaching an ultra-short-throw projector (the Epson BrightLink 595Wi) to this for projecting maps, foam/leather armor and sewing patterns, and other large-scale images for tracing onto a table. The monitor weighs 12.1 lbs. Slightly different weight distribution in that than in a monitor, but still noteworthy IMO that something of that weight (within advertised specs) could not stay up. What I did: 1. Unscrewed the tilt mount section entirely, saving the hardware that held it in place, and fully removed it from the end of the arm 2. After attaching the VESA mount plate to the projector, aligned the mount for the back of the projector with the hole for the tilt 3. Used the original hardware to bolt the VESA plate directly to the arm Thankfully, this worked exactly for my needs. Since I mounted this projector above my work table, the main priority was to be able to keep the projector suspended at a consistent height in a small footprint without slipping, dropping, or being bumped while cutting things out. The rest of the monitor arm is perfect for that; it's held the right height for the past two weeks, and the clamp is very secure without damaging my table. The spacers and bolts that came with this arm also worked great with the VESA adapter to hold up the projector. If anyone reading this is doing a similar setup for projectors (or using a VESA adapter at all), my advice: make sure any nuts, bolts, etc. are the correct size. This monitor arm's VESA plate takes 4mm screws to attach to monitors, but the VESA adapter I got only had 6mm and 8mm hardware in it. I had to get a set of 4mm washers to put on the end of this arm's provided screws, in order to attach the "plate" end of the VESA adapter arms effectively.
Works great for what I needed. Easy assembly
